categories.name: Extreme Physical Tension & Exertion
categories.description: The actor begins in a state of calm, sensory awareness, or gentle focus — then erupts into full-body muscular strain. Words are squeezed out between clenched teeth, punctuated by grunts and trembling breath, as the body approaches or exceeds its physical limits.

subcategories.name: Impossible Lifts
subcategories.description: Lifting objects of catastrophic weight — vehicles, collapsed structures, industrial machinery — usually to save a life or escape danger. The actor must convey the progressive failure of the body under gravitational force.
example_scenarios: Lifting the rear axle of a car off a child's pinned leg in a parking lot
Hoisting a collapsed ceiling beam off a trapped firefighter
Deadlifting a refrigerator that fell on a toddler in a kitchen
Raising a garage door that came down on a neighbor's arm
Flipping a capsized ATV off a pinned hiking partner
Pulling a fallen tree trunk off a wounded deer hunter
Lifting a submerged dock anchor to free a caught fishing line tangled around a friend's ankle
Raising the hood of a collapsed industrial press off a factory worker
Hoisting a collapsed barn door off a horse that's still breathing
Lifting a piano that slid off a truck ramp onto a moving crew member

subcategories.name: Pulling Against Immovable Forces
subcategories.description: Dragging, hauling, or pulling something that will not yield — rope tug-of-war at survival scale, pulling a vehicle out of mud, hauling a net full of catch. The strain is horizontal and relentless, voice fracturing under the sustained pull.
example_scenarios: Pulling a rope attached to a dock to stop a boat drifting into rocks in a storm
Hauling a drowning horse out of a mud pit by its halter
Dragging an unconscious soldier out of a burning vehicle by the collar
Pulling a stuck truck out of a snowdrift using a tow chain alone
Hauling a full crab trap up from fifty feet of depth in freezing water
Dragging a cast-iron anchor hand-over-hand from the ocean floor
Pulling a collapsed section of tent pole through wet canvas in a hurricane
Hauling a loaded ore cart up a mine shaft incline by hand
Dragging a waterlogged canoe over a portage trail through dense brush
Pulling a sled loaded with supplies through chest-deep snow at altitude

subcategories.name: Pushing Beyond Capacity
subcategories.description: Pressing or driving something that resists completely — a jammed door, a sliding vehicle, a machine that won't yield. The voice comes out in explosive bursts timed to each push, degrading into continuous strained vocalization.
example_scenarios: Pushing a car out of the path of an incoming train with seconds to spare
Pressing a flooded bulkhead door closed on a sinking submarine
Pushing a stuck elevator car up to floor level by hand from below
Driving a sofa barricade against a door as someone slams into it from the other side
Pushing a rolled truck back onto its wheels on an icy mountain road
Pressing a warped safe room door shut against a tornado's pressure differential
Shoving a stalled ambulance out of an intersection during a cardiac emergency
Pushing a collapsed barn wall upright to free cattle
Pressing a stuck flood gate closed as water rises around the operator's waist
Driving a loading dock door shut against hurricane-force wind

subcategories.name: Straining Against Restraints
subcategories.description: Bound, cuffed, trapped in wreckage — the actor strains against ropes, zip ties, handcuffs, or structural debris with every muscle, voice becoming raw and desperate as flesh tears against the restraint.
example_scenarios: Straining zip-tied wrists apart behind a radiator in an abandoned warehouse
Pulling against handcuffs attached to a steering wheel as floodwater rises
Twisting out of rope restraints on a chair as smoke fills the room
Wrenching a trapped foot free from collapsed scaffolding as it shifts
Yanking a seatbelt that won't release after a rollover crash
Pulling a caught hand free from industrial machinery before it cycles again
Straining against a bungee cord tied around the wrists during a hazing ordeal
Wrenching against a leg iron chained to a wall as the building catches fire
Pulling an arm free from quicksand-like mud before losing consciousness
Breaking zip ties binding the ankles on the edge of a moving vehicle

subcategories.name: Isometric Death Holds
subcategories.description: Holding a position under catastrophic load with no movement possible — supporting a ledge, bracing a collapsing structure, holding a rope above a drop. The actor holds the line, voice shaking with sustained muscular failure.
example_scenarios: Bracing a collapsing mine shaft ceiling with both arms while others crawl out
Holding a rope attached to a climber dangling over a crevasse until rescuers arrive
Supporting a collapsed porch roof above an elderly woman on both hands
Gripping a helicopter skid with both hands while hanging above the ocean
Holding a bridge support cable while a repair crew reconnects the anchor
Bracing a flood barrier with the body against surging water pressure
Holding an overloaded stretcher horizontal on a steep mountain descent
Supporting the weight of a child on an outstretched arm above broken glass
Gripping a boat's lifeline with one hand while the vessel rolls in storm swells
Holding a split beam in position while a trapped person is extracted below

subcategories.name: Combat Grappling & Submission
subcategories.description: Physical combat that requires total muscular engagement — wrestling, choking, pinning, breaking free. The actor's speech is interrupted by exertion, impact, and the savage intimacy of body-to-body struggle.
example_scenarios: Breaking a chokehold from behind in a dark alley with full explosive effort
Pinning a larger attacker to the ground while calling for help
Escaping a mount position on the floor of a burning building
Forcing an armed wrist down against resistance to prevent a shooting
Wrestling a knife away from an attacker using both hands and body weight
Breaking free from a rear bear hug while ribs compress
Choking out an opponent who outweighs by fifty pounds in a survival scenario
Forcing a door open against someone pushing from the other side with full body
Pulling an attacker off a third person while absorbing their resistance
Struggling to maintain a joint lock on a panicking, adrenaline-flooded opponent

subcategories.name: Sprint & Explosive Effort
subcategories.description: Pure explosive muscular output — sprinting, jumping, climbing at maximum velocity. The dialogue is delivered mid-exertion, syllables timed to footfalls, voice rattling with impact and effort.
example_scenarios: Sprinting full speed down a collapsing mine tunnel ahead of the cave-in
Climbing a chain-link fence at maximum speed to escape a guard dog
Running across a burning building's floor to reach a window before collapse
Sprinting through chest-deep snow to reach a child who fell through ice
Climbing a rope ladder on a moving helicopter with wind and noise chaos
Running up seven flights of fire stairs carrying a fire extinguisher
Sprinting down a ship's deck as it lists sharply to one side
Climbing out of a capsizing kayak and swimming hard for shore
Jumping between rooftops in pursuit, landing and recovering in motion
Sprinting the final stretch of a grueling mountain ultramarathon at the limit

subcategories.name: Trapped in Machinery or Wreckage
subcategories.description: Pinned by mechanical or structural force — wedged in wreckage, caught in gears, trapped under vehicles. The actor speaks in the voice of someone whose thorax is compressed and whose every word costs oxygen.
example_scenarios: Pinned under a collapsed warehouse shelf with a forklift approach getting closer
Wedged in the crumpled driver's seat of an overturned truck with the door jammed
Caught between two closing industrial press plates with millimeters to spare
Pinned against a wall by a runaway shopping cart loaded with concrete blocks
Trapped in collapsed bleachers with steel tubing across the chest
Wedged in a drainage pipe during a flash flood with rising water
Pinned under a toppled hospital bed in an earthquake with staff trying to lift it
Caught in a grain auger that's pulled the sleeve before the kill switch is hit
Trapped between the car and the garage wall as the car rolls on a slope
Pinned under a fallen stage lighting rig that's still sparking electricity

subcategories.name: Tug-of-War with Death
subcategories.description: Holding on to someone or something that is being pulled away by gravity, current, or force — keeping a grip while strength fails. The actor must voice the deterioration of grip and the terror of imminent loss.
example_scenarios: Gripping a child's wrist dangling from a cliff edge as grip slowly fails
Holding a partner's hand as they're pulled by a riptide current
Clutching a rope attached to a dog being swept downstream
Keeping hold of a stretcher handle as a helicopter lurches in turbulence
Gripping someone's collar as they slide toward open elevator shaft
Holding onto a fire escape railing while dangling above a six-story drop
Keeping grip on a steering wheel as power steering fails at high speed
Clutching a boat rail as a wave breaks over the stern and tries to sweep a crew member overboard
Holding the handle of a gurney on a steep ramp that starts to roll
Gripping a partner's ankle as they're pulled into a collapsed crawlspace

subcategories.name: Endurance at the Edge of Collapse
subcategories.description: The actor has been straining for a long time and is now at the terminal edge — shaking, vision narrowing, muscles giving out, still trying. The voice is ragged, stripped of control, but still pushing words through the wreckage of the body.
example_scenarios: The final kilometers of a solo Arctic crossing, hauling a full sled, barely upright
Hour six of treading water after a sailing accident waiting for rescue
Holding a stress position in a POW interrogation, refusing to break
The last ascent of a fourteen-thousand-foot peak with severe altitude sickness
Completing a military selection obstacle course after three days without sleep
The final lap of an open-water swim in frigid conditions
End-stage of a strongman competition deadlift event at personal maximum
The last pitch of a solo free-climb with forearms pumped to failure
Finishing a wildfire hotshot shift after sixteen hours of line cutting
Completing a manual CPR cycle after thirty minutes with no mechanical assist and two responders down

categories.name: Extreme Breathlessness
categories.description: The actor begins in a state of calm, full-breath awareness — perhaps a meditative stillness, a slow exhale of pleasure, a moment of quiet observation. Then the air is stripped away. Words arrive in ragged fragments, gasped syllables, incomplete sentences where the inhale is louder than the words themselves.

subcategories.name: Post-Sprint Oxygen Debt
subcategories.description: The collapse after maximum cardiovascular exertion — the lungs demanding more than the world can supply. Speech is delivered between enormous gasping breaths, voice pitched high with effort, sentences broken by involuntary inhales.
example_scenarios: Just finished a full sprint across a burning airfield to reach the last departing aircraft
Reached the top of a fire escape after sprinting twelve floors with gear
Completed a 400-meter sprint to stop someone from jumping from a bridge
Just outran a military guard dog across a flooded compound
Finished a desperate uphill run to flag down an ambulance on a mountain road
Just sprinted the length of a hospital corridor to reach an emergency code
Reached a child trapped on a collapsing pier after a full-speed beach sprint
Just ran from a wildfire front across a quarter mile of open meadow
Finished a desperate race to catch a runaway horse before it reached a highway
Just sprinted through airport security to stop someone at the gate

subcategories.name: Near-Drowning & Water Inhalation
subcategories.description: Surfaces after breathing water — the lungs spasming, body purging fluid through coughing, voice wet and strangled as air fights its way back into flooded passages.
example_scenarios: Dragged to the surface after a riptide pulls under and holds for thirty seconds
Surfaces under a capsized kayak, finally finds the air pocket, gasping
Pulled from a frozen lake by bystanders after falling through ice
Rescued from a submerged car by a diver, choking water out on the riverbank
Survives a near-drowning in a rip current and collapses on a beach
Dragged up from a hotel pool after a seizure, staff performing rescue breathing
Pulled from a flooding basement as the last air pocket disappears
Surfaces during a scuba equipment failure after breathing partial water
Rescued from a storm surge that pinned against a seawall and submerged
Pulled out of a waterfall's hydraulic trap after circulating for forty seconds

subcategories.name: Severe Asthma Attack
subcategories.description: The airways narrow to almost nothing — each inhale a whistling desperate pull, each word costing oxygen that the lungs can barely absorb. The actor must convey the claustrophobia of being unable to breathe inside a functioning body.
example_scenarios: Sudden onset asthma attack in a dusty barn with no inhaler present
Exercise-induced attack during a military fitness test with a superior watching
Smoke-triggered severe attack inside a burning building evacuation
Allergen exposure at an outdoor wedding causes attack with inhaler in the car
Cat dander attack in a new partner's apartment before a first date
Mold exposure in a flooded house triggers the worst attack in years
Cold air attack during a winter marathon at mile twenty
Pollen-triggered severe attack during a hiking trip far from medication
Stress-induced attack during a high-stakes job interview with no rescue inhaler
Attack triggered by chemical fumes in a laboratory accident

subcategories.name: Choking on Food or Foreign Object
subcategories.description: The airway is suddenly and completely blocked — the actor moves from pleasurable eating or casual speech to total panic as nothing moves through the throat. Words are replaced by the desperate sounds of a body fighting for air.
example_scenarios: A piece of steak lodges in the throat at a romantic anniversary dinner
Inhales a vitamin capsule that catches sideways in the upper airway
A chunk of hard candy blocks the airway while driving alone on the highway
Bone from a fish fillet lodges transversely in the throat during a solo meal
A grape inhaled while laughing completely blocks the airway
A piece of unchewed meat blocks while eating alone at a late-night diner
A foreign object from a child's toy accidentally inhaled by the parent
A large pill swallowed dry lodges at the pharynx and won't move
A mouthful of food swallowed mid-laugh creates a complete blockage
A chunk of dry bread eaten too fast completely occludes the airway

subcategories.name: Hyperventilation & Panic Spiral
subcategories.description: The breathing accelerates beyond control — CO2 depletes, extremities tingle, vision narrows, and the body begins to lock up. The actor is caught in the feedback loop of terror and breath, voice cycling up into pure hyperventilating panic.
example_scenarios: Trapped in a collapsed elevator hyperventilating as the walls seem to close in
Panic attack on an aircraft during extreme turbulence mid-ocean
PTSD-triggered hyperventilation in a crowded stadium after a firecracker pops
Hyperventilating in a parking garage after narrowly escaping an assault
Spiral triggered by a phone call delivering a terminal diagnosis
Locked in a supply closet by mistake and descending into claustrophobic panic
First responder hyperventilating after a mass casualty scene overwhelms
Hyperventilation spiral in a confined MRI machine during a medical emergency
Panic-induced hyperventilation before a solo skydive at the aircraft door
Hyperventilating in a police interview room after being wrongly accused

subcategories.name: Altitude Sickness & Oxygen Starvation
subcategories.description: The oxygen simply isn't there — each breath accomplishes less, the mind fogs, the body moves in slow motion, but the actor still tries to communicate across the altitude barrier.
example_scenarios: Summit push on K2 at 8,600 meters with supplemental oxygen running out
Sudden ascent in a military aircraft with a failed pressurization system
Pilot hypoxia at cruising altitude with oxygen equipment failure
Altitude sickness onset during acclimatization on Denali at high camp
Hiker at 14,000 feet with no acclimatization and exertion-induced HACE
Hot air balloon emergency ascent above operational altitude in an emergency
Ski patrol responder called to 13,500 feet after a day at sea level
Construction worker on a high-altitude dam project in the Andes
Unpressurized WWII bomber mission at 25,000 feet with oxygen line cut by flak
High-altitude helicopter rescue at 18,000 feet with doors open

subcategories.name: Smoke Inhalation
subcategories.description: The lungs fill with toxic gas and particulates — the throat burns, voice goes ragged and hoarse, coughing interrupts every phrase, and the world narrows to the next breath.
example_scenarios: Trapped in a smoke-filled corridor looking for a fire exit in a hotel
Inside a vehicle that has caught fire with stuck seatbelt and filling smoke
Wildfire smoke overrun with a shelter-in-place barely holding
House fire rescuer without SCBA who went in anyway to pull out occupants
Structural fire collapse with smoke entering the survival void rapidly
Industrial chemical fire with smoke that burns the airway instantly
Low-oxygen smoke environment in a ship's engine room fire
Sealed room with a fire on the other side slowly filling with carbon monoxide
Warehouse fire during an overnight security shift with no alarm triggered
Cooking fire that fills an apartment and traps an elderly resident

subcategories.name: Panic-Induced Breathlessness from Threat
subcategories.description: Not exertion but pure sympathetic nervous system response — the body floods with adrenaline and the breath becomes impossible to regulate. The actor must navigate between the need to be silent and the body's demand to hyperventilate.
example_scenarios: Hiding in a closet from an intruder, trying to control breathing while terrified
Crouching behind a car as an active shooter passes feet away
Under a bed in a home invasion, body shaking, trying not to breathe audibly
Pressed against a wall in a warzone alley as boots approach in the dark
Hiding in tall grass from a predator animal that is hunting by sound
Frozen on a ledge above a thousand-foot drop, afraid to move or breathe
Inside a shipping container that's being loaded and darkness closes in
Crouched in a swamp under a dock as a patrol boat sweeps overhead
Pressed into the corner of an elevator when the power cuts and a stranger is present
Holding breath behind a dumpster after a street confrontation escalates

subcategories.name: Medical Respiratory Emergency
subcategories.description: Pulmonary embolism, anaphylaxis, pneumothorax — the body loses the ability to breathe through pathology rather than environment. The actor is aware something is catastrophically wrong inside, and the voice reflects the slow horror of losing breath from within.
example_scenarios: Pulmonary embolism onset mid-flight over the Atlantic with no doctor aboard
Anaphylactic throat closure after an unexpected nut exposure at a dinner party
Spontaneous pneumothorax in the middle of a work presentation
Tension pneumothorax developing after a workplace injury with no medical help nearby
Severe allergic asthma triggered by bee sting in a remote wilderness area
Epiglottitis onset in an adult, airway closing faster than help can arrive
Post-operative respiratory depression waking alone in a recovery room
Drug reaction causing bronchospasm in an outpatient procedure with staff absent
Laryngeal edema developing after insect sting on a solo camping trip
Pulmonary edema from flash drowning event, lungs filling slowly after rescue

subcategories.name: Underwater Endurance & Free Diving Panic
subcategories.description: The breath hold reaches its limit — CO2 builds, the diaphragm contracts involuntarily, the lungs beg for air, and the surface is still out of reach. The actor speaks at the edge of blackout, words fragmenting under oxygen depletion.
example_scenarios: Free diver at sixty feet on a breath hold when a current changes direction
Trapped under ice with one small air pocket that is rapidly depleting
Navy SEAL combat dive going past safe bottom time without realizing it
Competitive free diver approaching static apnea world record, losing control
Caught under a wave set with lungs already half-depleted from the last hold
Cave diver whose light fails at the farthest penetration point on a breath hold
Spearfisherman tangled in kelp at twenty meters on a long breath hold
Underwater photographer who misjudges depth and current simultaneously
Pearl diver in traditional practice, rope tangled at bottom, cannot ascend
Research diver whose rebreather malfunctions at depth with long return swim

categories.name: Extreme Physical Pain
categories.description: The actor opens in a state of sensory richness — warmth, pleasure, presence, intimacy. Then the pain arrives. It may be sudden and catastrophic or escalating and inescapable. The voice moves through recognition, denial, and surrender — from articulate speech to pure vocalization, words dissolving into the primal language of agony.

subcategories.name: Gunshot Wounds
subcategories.description: The sudden trauma of ballistic impact — the body absorbs an energy transfer that the brain cannot immediately categorize. The actor moves from shock through blossoming pain, voice fragmenting under the weight of fresh mortal injury.
example_scenarios: Shot in the shoulder mid-sentence during a hostage negotiation
Taking a round to the thigh in a firefight while calling coordinates to a teammate
Gut shot in a robbery gone wrong, trying to reach a phone while alone
Shot through the hand while shielding someone else from a drive-by
Sniper round through the calf during a rooftop evacuation
Through-and-through shoulder wound in a police raid gone wrong
Accidental discharge at a gun range catches the foot, bullet through bone
Shot while wearing a vest — blunt trauma fractures ribs through the armor
Graze wound across the temple that splits skin to bone during a firefight
Multiple fragment wounds from a grenade detonation at fifteen feet

subcategories.name: Severe Burns
subcategories.description: Chemical or thermal burn that strips the nerve endings before they die — the most exquisite pain the nervous system produces. The actor voices the escalating arc from contact to full-thickness burn agony.
example_scenarios: Molten metal splash from a foundry ladle across the forearm
Chemical burn from industrial acid spill on the torso and upper chest
Flash burn from an explosion at a gas station across the face and hands
Boiling water kettle tipped over the lap in a kitchen fall
Steam pipe rupture in an industrial plant, pressurized steam across the back
Napalm-adjacent incendiary burn in a combat environment
Alkali burn from strong lye solution in a soap-making accident
Severe sunburn after falling asleep unprotected on a reflective salt flat
Electrical arc flash burn across the arms and face during utility work
Partial-thickness burns from a wildfire overrun that caught a firefighter

subcategories.name: Compound Fractures & Broken Bones
subcategories.description: Bone breaking through skin, limbs bending where they should not — the voice captures both the initial fracture shock and the nauseating sustained pain of displaced bone under pressure.
example_scenarios: Tibia shatters on impact during a motorcycle crash, bone visible
Forearm snapped mid-shaft in a football tackle gone wrong
Femur fracture in a ski accident far from the nearest lift
Wrist compound fracture from a direct fall on concrete from a height
Collarbone shattered by a direct impact in a cycling collision
Multiple rib fractures from a car door closing on the torso in a crash
Pelvis fracture from a horse kick while working with livestock
Ankle compound fracture after falling through a rotten wooden floor
Vertebral fracture in a construction site fall, still partially mobile
Hand crushed in heavy machinery, multiple metacarpals fractured

subcategories.name: Impalement & Penetrating Wounds
subcategories.description: A foreign object enters the body and stays there — the actor must voice the difference between the initial puncture and the sustained, three-dimensional pain of an object inside living tissue.
example_scenarios: Impaled on a rebar stake in a construction site fall, cannot remove it
Pitchfork tine through the thigh in a farm accident
Fence post through the chest cavity after a vehicular accident off-road
Knife wound to the abdomen in a street confrontation, blade still inside
Arrow through the calf in a hunting accident from a misfire
Steel rod through the shoulder from an industrial press failure
Shard of glass through the foot from a car windshield during a crash
Impaled through the hip on ornamental iron fence spikes after a fall
Drill bit through the palm in a shop class accident
Wood splinter, fist-sized, through the forearm from an explosion

subcategories.name: Animal Attacks
subcategories.description: The body is seized, bitten, lacerated, or crushed by an animal — the actor must convey both the mechanical violence of being prey and the specific horror of being held inside a living force.
example_scenarios: Mountain lion bite on the back of the skull during a trail run
Bull shark bite on the lower leg during a surf session
Grizzly bear mauling attack on the arms and torso during a trail encounter
Pit bull locked on the forearm with full crushing pressure
Alligator death roll on the ankle in a Florida waterway
Rattlesnake strike to the hand while reaching into a rock crevice
Wild boar tusk goring the inner thigh during a hunting trip
Moose stomp attack — hooves coming down on the ribcage and shoulder
Bark scorpion sting to the face and neck with full venom delivery
Box jellyfish tentacle wrap around both legs in the open ocean

subcategories.name: Electrocution
subcategories.description: Electricity seizes the body — muscles lock, the heart lurches, pain radiates from the entry wound to every nerve ending simultaneously. The actor cannot voluntarily release the source; every syllable is forced through locked jaw and rigid throat.
example_scenarios: Hand locked to a live 240-volt wire in a home renovation accident
Lightning strike at close range — knocked off feet, hearing gone, burning
Power line falls across a car hood, contact through the door handle
Industrial 480-volt panel arc flash during maintenance work
Electric fence current sustained as a foot slips and cannot break contact
Taser deployment at maximum duration on bare skin by mistake in a training exercise
Submerged pool pump short circuit while treading water
Hand trapped on a faulty appliance with current and cannot release grip
Tower climber in contact with a live transmission line during a storm
Electrocution from a damaged extension cord in standing flood water

subcategories.name: Surgical and Medical Agony
subcategories.description: Pain administered by the medical system — procedures that go wrong, insufficient anesthesia, field surgery without supplies. The actor must voice the obscene intimacy of clinical pain delivered by hands intended to heal.
example_scenarios: Anesthesia awareness during an open abdominal surgery, paralyzed but conscious
Field amputation of a crushed limb with only improvised pain management
Bone marrow biopsy in which the local anesthetic is insufficient
Wound debridement of a severe burn in a field hospital without adequate sedation
Dental extraction of a badly abscessed molar with failing local block
Chest tube insertion to relieve a pneumothorax in an emergency without enough lidocaine
Dislocated shoulder manual reduction with minimal sedation in a remote clinic
Fracture manipulation and splinting in the field on an expedition
Deep wound irrigation and suturing in a wilderness first-aid scenario
Interrupted epidural during a prolonged labor complication

subcategories.name: Crush Injuries
subcategories.description: The body is compressed under weight — an avalanche, collapsed debris, industrial crush. The actor voices the slow, inescapable pressure of being squeezed by tons of world, ribs flexing, organs protesting.
example_scenarios: Trapped under rubble in an earthquake with torso partially compressed
Caught in an avalanche — compact snow hardening around the body
Arm pulled into industrial rollers in a paper mill accident
Lower body pinned under a collapsed stadium bleacher section
Hand inside a hydraulic press when the cycle triggers accidentally
Torso pinned between a backing truck and a loading dock wall
Leg trapped between two vehicles in a multi-car collision
Chest compressed under a collapsed retaining wall in a landslide
Hand in a car door as it slams closed with full force
Pinned under a heavy horse that falls during a trail ride

subcategories.name: Nerve and Chronic Pain Crisis
subcategories.description: The worst of chronic pain conditions in their acute episodes — trigeminal neuralgia, cluster headaches, CRPS flare. The actor voices pain that arrives from inside, with no external cause to orient against.
example_scenarios: Trigeminal neuralgia lightning strike mid-sentence on a date
Cluster headache onset described as an ice pick through the eye socket
CRPS full flare in a limb triggered by a temperature change
Kidney stone passage through the ureter during an important meeting
Endometriosis rupture during a physical exam
Sciatica nerve compression crisis with drop to the floor mid-conversation
Gallbladder attack with referred shoulder tip pain escalating rapidly
Aortic dissection onset — the tearing chest pain that moves to the back
Pancreatitis acute episode — the belt of agony around the midsection
Ruptured ovarian cyst with internal bleeding, pain spreading as peritonitis begins

subcategories.name: Torture and Extreme Deliberate Pain
subcategories.description: Pain applied by human hands with intent — the actor voices resistance, the attempt to maintain identity against systematic destruction of the body's comfort. The horror is in the slow, methodical nature of the assault.
example_scenarios: Fingernails being removed during a POW interrogation
Waterboarding — the drowning sensation applied deliberately and repeatedly
Stress position maintained for hours with guards ensuring no relief
Salt applied to open lacerations during an interrogation
Bones of the hand systematically broken one by one in an intelligence scenario
Sustained electrical current applied to bare feet in a detention scenario
Forced physical exertion to total collapse in a rendition scenario
Deliberate burning with a cigarette in a hostage situation
Sustained blunt trauma applied to the soles of the feet
Sleep deprivation combined with physical stress positions over seventy-two hours

categories.name: Extreme Temperature Shock
categories.description: The actor begins in thermal comfort — a warm bath, cool shade, the pleasant sensation of moderate temperature against skin. Then the thermal assault arrives. The voice documents what happens to the human instrument under extreme cold or heat: teeth chatter, breath crystallizes, speech slurs with hypothermia, or words arrive in scorched bursts between desperate cooling attempts.

subcategories.name: Ice Water Immersion
subcategories.description: The body submerged in near-freezing water — the cold shock response, the hyperventilation, the progressive loss of muscle function. The actor voices the stages: gasp, panic, slurring control, hypothermic drift.
example_scenarios: Falling through lake ice in winter while crossing on foot
Ice bucket challenge taken to extreme — full submersion in an ice bath
Cold water therapy plunge pool session that goes too long
Capsized in a glacial river during a kayaking descent in early spring
Dropped into a frozen ocean after a shipwreck in Arctic waters
Falling into a frozen quarry pool while taking photographs at the edge
Military SERE training cold water immersion phase
Avalanche victim partially buried in slush and ice meltwater for hours
Jumping into a spring-fed swimming hole in April, water still four degrees
Search and rescue swimmer entering freezing ocean to reach a capsized vessel

subcategories.name: Polar Storm Exposure
subcategories.description: Wind chill below minus forty, frostbite developing on extremities, the voice struggling to form words through frozen jaw and stiff lips. The actor conveys the progressive shutdown of the body's communication systems under cold.
example_scenarios: Stranded on an Antarctic research traverse in a white-out blizzard
Lost in a Siberian taiga winter storm with inadequate gear
Summit storm on Everest at the South Col with no shelter
Car breaks down on an isolated Canadian highway in a minus-forty cold snap
Mountaineer bivouacked without a sleeping bag above 7,000 meters in a storm
Overnight exposure in Minnesota backcountry after a snowshoe accident
Polar expedition member whose tent collapses in a katabatic wind event
Rescue team member operating in a wind chill of minus sixty on a mountain search
Sailor overboard in the North Sea in January, in the water for twenty minutes
Trail runner caught above treeline in a sudden Rocky Mountain whiteout

subcategories.name: Scalding Water Burns
subcategories.description: Boiling or near-boiling liquid contacting the skin — the initial shock, the delayed blooming of searing pain as the nerve endings respond, the ongoing burning sensation that is worse seconds after contact.
example_scenarios: Knocking a full pot of boiling pasta water off the stove onto the feet and legs
Steam from a pressure cooker venting directly onto the face and hands
Scalding coffee spilled across the lap at freeway speed in a moving vehicle
Industrial steam pipe failure — a jet of 150-degree steam across the torso
Hot oil splash from a deep fryer during a kitchen fire
Boiling water geyser eruption in a geothermal area stepping off the path
Scalding tap water in an old building's shower with a failed pressure valve
Hot spring fall — surface looks safe, temperature is eighty-five degrees Celsius
Baking tray pulled from the oven contacts both forearms simultaneously
Pressure washer with hot water setting contacting bare skin at full pressure

subcategories.name: Desert Heat Stroke
subcategories.description: The body overheating from the inside — core temperature rising past forty-one degrees, the brain starting to misfire, the voice going strange and dissociated as thermoregulation fails.
example_scenarios: Dehydrated hiker in Death Valley at peak summer heat, disoriented and collapsing
Marathon runner hitting heat stroke at mile twenty in a humid southern summer
Roofer in Arizona August sun with no shade break since seven a.m.
Military marching exercise in Saudi Arabia in summer, one soldier going down
Music festival attendee in a sealed tent area on a hot July afternoon
Agricultural worker in Imperial Valley during a heat emergency with no water
Cyclist bonking in the Mojave Desert with empty bottles and no shade
Homeless person in a Phoenix summer heatwave with nowhere to shelter
Construction worker on a black asphalt project in Texas in July
Ultramarathon runner in Badwater 135, core temperature reaching critical level

subcategories.name: Fire Exposure and Burning
subcategories.description: Direct contact with open flame — clothing catching fire, hair igniting, skin blistering. The actor voices the primal terror of being on fire and the sensory overwhelm of burning alive.
example_scenarios: Sleeve catching fire from a fireplace and flames climbing the arm
Kitchen grease fire engulfs the cook's hands and torso
Wildfire overrun of a dozer operator who deploys a fire shelter
Stunt performer whose flame protection fails during a full-body burn take
Campfire explosion from accelerant poured on dying coals
Hair catching fire from a birthday candle leaning too close
Clothing ignition from an arc flash in an electrical substation
Trapped in a burning vehicle with door jammed as flames reach the cabin
Factory worker's clothing ignition from a chemical flash fire
Flamethrower training accident in a military scenario with proximity error

subcategories.name: Cryogenic and Industrial Cold Exposure
subcategories.description: Extreme cold beyond ordinary winter — liquid nitrogen, cryogenic storage leaks, industrial freezer accidents. The cold is so extreme it causes burns. The actor voices the paradox of freezing and burning simultaneously.
example_scenarios: Liquid nitrogen spill onto the forearms in a laboratory accident
Industrial freezer door jammed shut during a solo stock check
Cryotherapy chamber malfunction holding the temperature below safe limits
Dry ice packed around a cargo shipment contacts bare skin during handling
Liquid oxygen contact on the skin during an aerospace maintenance error
Cold storage warehouse lock failure, trapped inside at minus twenty
Refrigerant leak in an enclosed mechanical room reaches toxic and extreme cold
Meat locker door failure on a trawler in the Bering Sea in winter
Medical professional accidentally contacts liquid helium in a lab dewar failure
Firefighter's glove torn off in a cryogenic gas suppression system activation

subcategories.name: Hyperthermia in Enclosed Spaces
subcategories.description: Trapped in a hot car, a sauna gone wrong, an industrial oven, a shipping container in summer. The heat builds without escape and the actor voices the progressive cognitive and physical degradation of severe hyperthermia.
example_scenarios: Trapped in a parked car in summer with windows jammed and door locks failed
Sauna session with a jammed door, temperature climbing past one hundred degrees
Industrial oven proximity — maintenance worker trapped in a hot conveyor tunnel
Shipping container in a Arizona rail yard in July with partial ventilation
Server room with failed cooling during a summer surge, trapped inside
Greenhouse in July with a stuck door and full sun on glass panels
Laundry room on a cruise ship near the boiler intake with door jammed
Racehorse transport trailer broken down in Texas summer heat
HVAC worker in a ceiling crawlspace in Florida with no ventilation access
Military vehicle with broken air conditioning in a desert operation in August

subcategories.name: Frostbite Onset and Extremity Loss
subcategories.description: The fingers, toes, nose, ears going numb and then dead — the strange painlessness of early frostbite giving way to the agonizing rewarm, the actor voicing the horror of watching the body disconnect from itself.
example_scenarios: Climber on Everest removing a glove to operate a camera, then unable to feel fingers
Night rescue team member with boots soaked through in minus twenty weather
Homeless person waking with frostbitten feet after a winter shelter is full
Polar expedition skier discovering blackened toes at a rest stop
Soldier in a winter trench with immersion foot developing into frostbite
Ice climbing belayer stationary for four hours in minus thirty conditions
Research scientist in an Antarctic field station whose heating system fails
Snowmobile accident victim waiting for rescue with no emergency gear
Winter hiker who stops moving and sits on snow with wet clothing
Child lost in a winter storm, found with white, waxy facial frostbite

subcategories.name: Thermal Shock Contrast
subcategories.description: The body subjected to sudden extreme temperature transition — jumping from a sauna into ice water, an industrial temperature shock chamber, or sudden cold exposure after overheating. The vocal cords seize in the transition.
example_scenarios: Nordic sauna tradition — jumping from a hundred-degree sauna into a frozen lake
Industrial temperature testing chamber cycling an engineer from plus eighty to minus thirty
Cold shower taken at full cold after extreme heat exposure to prevent heat stroke
Firefighter emerging from a burning building into an exterior air temperature of minus fifteen
Athletes undergoing contrast hydrotherapy at extreme temperature differentials
Diver surfacing from warm tropical water into an Antarctic-style air temperature inversion
Worker in a frozen food facility moving from the blast freezer to the heat seal room
Participant in a cryotherapy clinic moving immediately to a steam room incorrectly
Desert military operator moving from a hundred-degree external to a cryogenic first aid treatment
Cooking competition contestant reaching into a commercial freezer immediately after oven work

subcategories.name: Fever Crisis and Internal Heat
subcategories.description: The body burning from the inside — fever above 41 degrees, the voice hallucinatory and slick, words emerging from a state between waking and delirium, the body's own heat becoming the enemy.
example_scenarios: Malaria crisis fever in a remote jungle camp with no medication remaining
Sepsis fever spiking to forty-two degrees in a hospital room overnight
Heat stroke combined with viral infection driving fever to critical levels
Child's febrile convulsion onset in the middle of the night
Post-surgery infection fever reaching crisis point with no nursing check-in
Untreated appendicitis abscess rupturing with fever spiking simultaneously
Military recruit with untreated heat injury developing systemic fever
Meningitis fever onset — the rash appearing and the temperature climbing
Flu-related febrile delirium in an elderly person living alone
Dengue hemorrhagic fever crisis in a traveler without access to care

categories.name: Extreme Oral & Gustatory Sensation
categories.description: The actor begins in a state of sensory anticipation — the pleasure of food, the warmth of a drink, the comfort of the mouth as the most intimate sensory organ. Then the oral assault arrives. The voice becomes wet, distorted, interrupted by involuntary sounds — coughing, gagging, the hiss of pain, words mangled by a mouth that is on fire, frozen, overwhelmed, or chemically attacked.

subcategories.name: Superhot Chili and Capsaicin Overload
subcategories.description: The mouth encountering capsaicin at the level of Carolina Reapers, Pepper X, or concentrated extract — the burning spreading from lips to throat to stomach, eyes streaming, voice going broken and wet.
example_scenarios: Biting into a Carolina Reaper without knowing what it is at a cookout
A chip challenge with a single chip coated in the world's hottest extract
Eating a ghost pepper on a dare with no dairy available to neutralize
Restaurant hot sauce prank — bottle swapped with a million-Scoville extract
Competitive chili eating where the last dish is a pure capsaicin reduction
Hot pepper eating contest at a county fair with escalating heat levels
Tasting a Trinidad Moruga Scorpion raw, skin and seeds included
Accidentally drinking a capsaicin extract used to deter bears
Spicy ramen challenge — the black level with a full spoonful of Reaper paste
Kimchi made with triple the normal gochugaru, fermented to peak heat

subcategories.name: Extreme Sourness
subcategories.description: The salivary glands fire, the face collapses, the jaw seizes — citric acid and malic acid at concentrations that physically hurt. The actor voices the involuntary facial convulsion and the weird pain-pleasure of extreme sour.
example_scenarios: Eating a Warheads extreme sour candy challenge — entire bag at once
Biting into a Seville orange without preparation, flesh and pith
Drinking a shrub vinegar cocktail without warning — pure concentrated acid
Tasting a fermented beverage with extreme lactic acid concentration
Eating a pickled green plum preserved in maximum salt and acid
Sour candy challenge — a full packet of the most extreme powder
Drinking kombucha during secondary fermentation overshoot — very high acidity
Raw tamarind eaten without sweetener, full sour pulp
Lemon juice shots — straight citric acid in rapid succession
Eating a persimmon before it's ripe, full astringency and acidity combined

subcategories.name: Scalding Food and Drink Burns
subcategories.description: Food or liquid too hot to safely consume, taken at peak temperature — the roof of the mouth, tongue, and throat burning with contact. The actor voices the delayed realization and cascading oral pain.
example_scenarios: Taking a large bite of fresh-from-the-oven pizza, cheese at peak molten temperature
Drinking coffee that's just come off the boil without waiting
A soup dumpling (xiao long bao) that ruptures and releases scalding broth
Hot chocolate drunk too fast in the cold, scalding the entire throat
Pulling a pot pie from the oven and eating the filling immediately
McDonald's hot coffee scenario — full cup spilled across the lap and hands
Eating ramen at the restaurant where it arrives still visibly boiling
Caramel sauce at caramelization temperature contacting the inside of the lip
Drinking tea poured directly from the kettle into a paper cup with no cooling
Molten cheese from a fondue pot that drops from the fork onto the tongue

subcategories.name: Extreme Bitterness and Poisonous Taste
subcategories.description: Tastes that the body reads as toxic — extreme bitterness triggering immediate gag reflex, tannins causing astringency that closes the throat, or actual accidental poisoning from a plant or chemical. The actor voices the body's emergency rejection response.
example_scenarios: Accidentally drinking isopropyl alcohol from a mislabeled container
Eating raw elderberries before processing, full toxic tannin content
Chewing on a raw bitter melon — the most bitter substance in common cuisine
Accidentally swallowing chloroquine tablets meant for an adult dose as a child
Tasting quinine sulfate powder directly — the bitterest substance measurable
Eating a raw bitter cucumber gone fully yellow with cucurbitacin
Drinking tonic water concentrate before dilution — pure quinine
Accidentally chewing a vitamin B12 with B complex — metallic and bitter
Eating raw dandelion greens with the full bitterness unmitigated
Accidentally consuming a mouthful of strong cold brew concentrate instead of water

subcategories.name: Wasabi and Horseradish Nasal Assault
subcategories.description: The sinuses ignite — the volatile isothiocyanates launching up through the nasal passage and detonating behind the eyes. The actor voices the involuntary vocalization and the strange upward-shooting pain that precedes the mouth fully processing the source.
example_scenarios: Eating a full portion of fresh wasabi from a Japanese restaurant without warning
Downing a wasabi bomb shot on a dare
Eating horseradish directly from the jar — a large spoonful
A sushi chef's error — full wasabi mound mistaken for avocado
Wasabi pea challenge — the ultra-concentrated version found at specialty stores
Real wasabi root grated fresh at a kaiseki meal — a thumb-sized mound
Horseradish in a Bloody Mary mixed at full competition strength
Chinese mustard from a dim sum restaurant — pure sinigrin assault
Sinus-clearing horseradish supplement taken at ten times the dose by accident
Wasabi ice cream from a novelty shop — the heat delayed and then overwhelming

subcategories.name: Brain Freeze and Ice Overload
subcategories.description: The sphenopalatine ganglion firing in response to cold — the ice cream headache that radiates from the palate to behind the eyes. The actor voices the weird, helpless agony of a pain that is produced by pleasure.
example_scenarios: Eating a Big Gulp slushie in one continuous pull on a hot day
Ice cream eating challenge — maximum speed for sixty seconds
Sipping a frozen margarita through a straw aimed directly at the upper palate
Eating a pint of ice cream straight from the freezer without tempering
A snow cone eaten at full speed at a summer carnival
Cold water waterfall swim — face and mouth submerged in glacial runoff
Slushie competition — two contestants racing to finish identical cups
A frozen cocktail at a beach bar — eaten in one mouthful as a show-off move
Ice cube held against the palate as a heat relief technique in summer
Drinking ice-cold water too fast after exercise on a hot day

subcategories.name: Extreme Oral Textures and Sensory Violations
subcategories.description: The mouth encountering textures that trigger the gag reflex or extreme revulsion — not taste but tactile oral sensation at the extreme. The actor voices the involuntary rejection response and the struggle to override it.
example_scenarios: Swallowing raw oysters that are still actively moving
Eating a live octopus with suckers attaching to the inside of the throat
Century egg eaten without preparation — the ammonia-sulfur combination
Eating natto for the first time — the slime, strings, and ammonia smell
Sea urchin gonads eaten raw for the first time — the iodine intensity
Fermented shark (hákarl) eaten at full pungency without nose holding
Durian flesh eaten in an enclosed space without prior exposure
Lutefisk in its most gelatinous form — the lye-cured fish texture
Raw liver eaten at room temperature as part of a survival scenario
Silkworm chrysalides in a Korean street food challenge

subcategories.name: Alcohol and Solvent Extremes
subcategories.description: High-proof spirits consumed straight, grain alcohol taken without dilution, or accidental exposure to non-beverage solvents. The actor voices the burning from lips to esophagus to stomach, the involuntary tears, the gasp of the airways.
example_scenarios: Drinking Everclear (190 proof) straight from the bottle for the first time
A Navy-strength rum shot — 57% ABV, taken neat and too fast
A whiskey challenge requiring shots of cask-strength single malt at 65%
Accidentally swallowing mouthwash at high alcohol concentration as a child
Drinking raw moonshine from an unlicensed still with methanol contamination risk
A cocktail challenge — the highest-proof cocktail the bar can legally serve
Absinthe at vintage concentration (68–80%) with no water dilution
Polish spirytus rektyfikowany taken in a shot challenge
High-proof rubbing alcohol accidentally swallowed in a first-aid kit mix-up
Home-brewed fruit wine with accidental sugar addition doubling the ABV

subcategories.name: Tooth and Jaw Pain During Eating
subcategories.description: The dental or jaw emergency mid-meal — biting down on an unexpected hard object, cracking a tooth, a filling dislodging, TMJ joint locking on a large bite. The actor voices the shattering surprise of oral skeletal pain.
example_scenarios: Biting down on an olive pit in a tapenade — the tooth cracks vertically
A fragment of ceramic from a broken bowl hidden in a meal — bites down hard
Cracking a molar on an unpopped popcorn kernel at a movie theater
A stone in a fig that contacts a root canal treated tooth
TMJ joint locking open mid-yawn while eating a large sandwich
Biting into frozen caramel that pulls a crown off completely
A filling that dislodges while eating sticky toffee pudding
A wisdom tooth fracturing on a particularly hard piece of sourdough crust
Ice chewing compulsion — a tooth shatters on a large ice cube
Biting into a whole chili thinking it's a mild pepper — capsaicin plus the crack

subcategories.name: Medical and Chemical Oral Procedures
subcategories.description: Oral sensations delivered by the medical or dental system — topical anesthetics going wrong, suction biopsy, the shock of a dental injection, bitter medication in liquid form. The actor voices the clinical intimacy of mouth-as-procedure-site.
example_scenarios: Dental injection into an abscess that is too inflamed for the anesthetic to work
Bitter chemotherapy oral rinse that triggers immediate nausea
Oral glucose tolerance test drink — maximum sugar concentration drunk on an empty stomach
Activated charcoal drink for poisoning — texture and volume overwhelming
Post-tonsillectomy pain during first attempt to swallow food
Dental extraction under-anesthesia — the pressure and cracking sensations
Oral biopsy punch removing tissue from the cheek mucosa
Swallowing a nasogastric tube — the involuntary gagging and the tube entering the throat
Liquid potassium supplement at high concentration — the metallic burning
Nitrous oxide dental procedure that creates extreme dissociation and oral numbness

categories.name: Extreme Surprise & Startle
categories.description: The actor is at peak vulnerability — relaxed, sensory, present, perhaps mid-thought or mid-pleasure. Then the startle arrives and the entire nervous system fires simultaneously. The voice goes from calm to primal in a single beat, then the actor must process the stimulus — relief, horror, grief, rage, or catatonic silence emerging from the ruins of that first total-body alarm response.

subcategories.name: Jump Scares and Sudden Appearance
subcategories.description: Someone or something appears without warning in a space the actor believed was safe — the classic startle template. The initial scream gives way to processing, and the emotional aftermath is as important as the initial response.
example_scenarios: A person standing silently in a dark corner of the bedroom when the light comes on
Turning from the kitchen sink to find a stranger inside the house
A face appearing at the window while doing dishes at night
Someone tapping the shoulder from behind in an empty office at midnight
A figure in the bathroom mirror that wasn't there before
A child's face appearing over the side of the bathtub while soaking
A colleague hiding in a locker room to prank a new hire — it goes wrong
A person sitting in the back seat discovered when checking the rearview mirror
A masked figure standing in the hallway when stumbling to the bathroom at three a.m.
A face appearing on the other side of a frosted glass door in a building thought to be empty

subcategories.name: Explosions and Sudden Loud Events
subcategories.description: The concussive physical impact of an unexpected explosion, gunshot, or sonic event that hits the body before the brain can process it. The actor voices the disorientation, tinnitus-adjacent silence, and the frantic reassembly of understanding.
example_scenarios: A transformer exploding on the street outside a window during a quiet morning
A gunshot fired inside a confined space during a robbery in progress
A firework detonating at ground level next to a crowd member
A sonic boom from a military jet over a suburban neighborhood without warning
A gas pipe explosion in an adjacent apartment while making coffee
A tire blowout at highway speed in the passenger seat of a car
A shotgun discharged indoors at close range during a confrontation
A thunderclap directly overhead after no audible approach in open country
An IED detonation near a convoy in a war zone — the ground lifting
A concert speaker stack toppling and crashing onto the stage during a set

subcategories.name: Discovering a Body or Catastrophic Scene
subcategories.description: Walking into a space and finding death, severe injury, or devastation that the mind was utterly unprepared for. The vocal response moves from the sharp intake of startle to the extended collapse of comprehension.
example_scenarios: Coming home to find a partner has died during the day — unexpectedly, in a chair
Opening a car trunk to retrieve luggage and finding a body inside
Walking into a workplace shooting aftermath before emergency services arrive
Discovering a child has fallen into a backyard pool and is motionless
Opening a storage unit rented from an estate sale and finding human remains
Coming back to a campsite to find it destroyed and a companion missing
Walking into the aftermath of a house fire that claimed the neighbors
Finding a crashed vehicle off a mountain road and recognizing the car
Discovering a colleague slumped over a desk unresponsive in a locked office
Walking into a barn to find an animal has given birth and died simultaneously

subcategories.name: Near-Miss Car Accidents
subcategories.description: The vehicle comes within inches of catastrophic collision and the body activates full sympathetic response before the danger fully passes. The actor voices the frozen instant and the shaking dissolution of adrenaline.
example_scenarios: A truck running a red light at full speed, passing inches in front of the hood
Brake failure on a mountain road — swerving and somehow stopping safely
A child running into the road, braking hard and stopping with centimeters to spare
A head-on near-miss on a foggy two-lane road, both vehicles pulling left simultaneously
A sudden blowout at 80 mph that fishtails the car back under control
Avoiding a multi-car pileup by using the shoulder and stopping in loose gravel
A pedestrian stepping off a curb who doesn't see the car until it passes them
Aquaplaning on a freeway, control lost and then miraculously recovered
A deer impact on a country road at night — the car survives, the actor doesn't know if the deer did
A bicycle courier cutting across traffic missing the mirror by less than an inch

subcategories.name: Devastating News Received Suddenly
subcategories.description: The phone call, the knock on the door, the word from the doctor's mouth that ends the world as it was. The actor's calm is structural and then the news shatters the foundation. The startle is internal — the soul recoiling from information.
example_scenarios: A call from a hospital while eating breakfast telling you a family member died
A doctor entering the consultation room with a specific face that communicates everything before speaking
A text message from a partner of ten years containing only four words ending the relationship
A call from the police at two a.m. asking to speak to the next of kin
The lawyer's face when reading the will and realizing what it contains
An employer calling to say the position has been eliminated effective immediately
A pregnancy test result arriving unexpectedly when none was expected
A message revealing that someone the actor trusted has been lying for years
A DNA test result delivering information about parentage that rewrites identity
A military notification team arriving at the door in dress uniform

subcategories.name: Intruder and Home Invasion Startle
subcategories.description: The home — the safest space — is revealed to be violated. Sounds in an empty house, evidence of presence, or the intruder in plain view. The actor voices the collapse of safety and the pure animal terror of being prey in one's own den.
example_scenarios: Hearing footsteps on the second floor while sitting alone on the ground floor
Finding the back door open that was locked when leaving three hours ago
A silhouette at the end of the hallway in the dark that doesn't belong to anyone living there
Waking to find someone standing at the foot of the bed in the dark
Coming home to find drawers opened and items moved but nothing obviously gone
A voice calling out from inside a house that was definitely empty on entry
Finding a window broken from the outside and glass inside on the floor
Seeing a light moving in a house through the window while locking the car outside
Realizing mid-shower that someone else is in the bathroom
Finding personal photographs left face-down on a kitchen counter that was bare when leaving

subcategories.name: Animal and Wildlife Encounters
subcategories.description: The sudden appearance of a dangerous animal at close range — the pure biological startle when the prey-predator circuit fires. The actor moves from calm to high-alert primal response in a single heartbeat.
example_scenarios: Stepping on a coiled rattlesnake on a dark path and feeling it move underfoot
A bear appearing six feet away around a blind corner on a hiking trail
Reaching into a bag to find a large spider has taken up residence
A bull shark appearing beneath while floating on a surfboard
Waking from sleep to find a large spider walking across the face
Finding a venomous snake in the bedding when pulling back the covers
A mountain lion appearing on a fence post at eye level in a suburban backyard
A wasp nest disturbed while reaching into a garden shed — full swarm response
A wild boar charging from dense brush on a morning run in rural France
A crocodile emerging from the water directly beneath feet while standing on a riverbank

subcategories.name: Medical Emergency Onset
subcategories.description: A medical crisis beginning without any warning — the person next to you having a seizure, a heart attack in a crowded restaurant, an anaphylactic reaction that no one expected. The actor voices the whiplash from social calm to emergency response.
example_scenarios: A companion having a grand mal seizure at the dinner table mid-conversation
A colleague collapsing face-first onto a keyboard in an open plan office
A child going limp and unresponsive in the arms for no apparent reason
Someone's allergic reaction visibly closing their throat at a restaurant
A fellow airplane passenger going gray and unconscious mid-flight
A runner collapsing at the finish line of a road race and not getting up
A stranger in a store having a cardiac arrest while reaching for a shelf item
A swimming companion who stops moving in the water without warning
A toddler who goes silent and blue during what seemed like routine fussing
A driver going unconscious at a red light in traffic next to the actor's car

subcategories.name: Structural Failure and Environmental Collapse
subcategories.description: The built world suddenly failing — a floor giving way, a ceiling coming down, a bridge trembling, a building beginning to shake. The actor voices the instant when the assumed permanence of the physical world is revealed as illusion.
example_scenarios: A floor giving way underfoot in an old building without warning
The first shock of a major earthquake striking while sitting indoors
A balcony railing failing while leaning against it on the tenth floor
A bridge making a sound that indicates structural failure underfoot mid-crossing
A tree falling across the road directly ahead while driving at speed
A ceiling section collapsing onto a desk one seat away in an office
A dam making a groan that signals imminent failure during inspection
A dock collapsing into the water while walking out to a boat
A ladder rung snapping at the top of a fifteen-foot extension
A cliff edge crumbling underfoot while looking out from a scenic overlook

subcategories.name: Digital and Information Shocks
subcategories.description: The modern-world startle — a notification, a message, a video, an image, a revelation delivered through a screen that triggers full-body physiological response. The actor is sitting in comfort and the horror arrives through a device.
example_scenarios: A video call showing something in the background of the other person's room that should not be there
An explicit video or photograph appearing in a work Slack channel by mistake
A news notification delivering a national catastrophe during a moment of total normalcy
A location ping from a partner's phone showing them somewhere they said they wouldn't be
A security camera notification showing someone inside an empty house
An email from a dead person's address — timestamped three minutes ago
A text message from an unknown number containing a photograph of the actor, taken today
A notification that all savings have been transferred out of a bank account
A social media notification showing a tagged photograph that should not exist
A voice message from an old phone backup playing through a speaker — a voice of someone who died
